Question: Can a narcissist be loyal?
Answer: A narcissist is only loyal to the moment and whatever feels "fun" to them. You're just a part of that "fun," and once you stop being entertaining or useful, their loyalty is gone. When I say "fun," I mean whatever the narcissist finds enjoyable, whether it's going to a new place with you, giving you the silent treatment on a special occasion, or teasing you until you cry. It’s all just a game to them. Narcissists are driven by their immature and selfish desires. They don’t want to grow, learn, or change because that would mean admitting they aren’t perfect. They don't care about your long-term goals, and they don't care about their own either. If something stops being fun for them, they'll drop it without a second thought. They find it amusing to mock your feelings, like when you worked hard to get them a new job, only for them to quit after a week and laugh at how upset you get. To them, that's the real fun. Question: Do narcissists have true friends?
Answer: At first, it may seem like narcissists have a lot of friends. They come across as charming, confident, and sociable, which attracts people to them. But these friendships are often not as real as they seem. Narcissists see relationships, including friendships, as a way to make themselves feel more important. They only care about what they can get from the friendship, like attention or admiration. This means their friendships are usually shallow and don't have deep emotional connections. These friendships also don't last very long. Narcissists don't have empathy and often manipulate or use people for their own benefit. This can lead to conflicts and the end of the friendship. Being friends with a narcissist can be difficult because they go back and forth between being really nice to you and then devaluing you if you can't make them feel important. It's also important to know that narcissists have a hard time seeing their own faults. They don't take responsibility for problems in their friendships and may blame others instead. This makes it hard to have a stable, long-lasting friendship with them. The fact that you are going to see through their lies, you're going to see through this and see exactly who they are. This is what they do, this is what they have done as children. They think that you are not going to see through it because they think that they are invincible, that they're these wonderful people that you are not going to see through. And that's, my friends, is their elevated ego, that they think no one is going to find out about. Question: What are the first signs of narcissistic abuse?
Answer: When your boundaries are tested. Healthier, "normal" people don't do this. It's a natural human instinct to pull back, like you've touched something hot, if you find yourself getting too close to violating someone else's boundaries. But narcissists don't react that way. The storm of their own emotions takes up all their attention. Getting what they want is all that matters to them. They think that satisfying their own desires is like a bandage to cover up their deep pain and self-esteem issues. But when you're driven by a huge amount of inner misery, you don't have the mental energy left to care about anyone else's wellbeing. Narcissists are always searching for a solution to their problems, but they'll never find it. Because they're looking for it outside of themselves, not within. They can't look inside, it's too dark and scary in there. They don't want to stir up what's really going on.
